title: Constructible finite stratification for separated flat quasi-finite morphisms
statement: Let X and U be schemes with X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let j : U ⟶ X be flat, locally of finite presentation, separated, and quasi-finite. Then there exists a finite locally closed stratification S of X whose strata are constructible and such that every pullback of j along a stratum immersion is finite.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ and its construction from the closed degree filtration

proof.text: The quasi-finite hypothesis supplies QuasiCompact j. Since X is quasi-compact, U is quasi-compact by QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace. Obtain local quasi-finiteness from isQuasiFinite_iff_isLocallyQuasiFinite_and_quasiCompact, then choose a uniform fibre-degree bound N using hasUniversallyBoundedFibers_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite.

Apply exists_closed_stratification_of_flat_quasiFinite to obtain the closed increasing filtration Z, its disjoint covering differences, universal finite-local-freeness property, and compact intersections with compact opens. Apply exists_flat_fp_lqf_bounded_stratification using N to obtain another closed increasing filtration B with B(N+1) equal to X and the same universal property.

For every x and degree r, test the two universal properties on X.fromSpecResidueField x, whose image is the singleton {x}. Membership of x in either degree-r difference is equivalent to the same assertion about the same pullback. Thus Z(r+1) minus Z(r) equals B(r+1) minus B(r). Monotonicity of B and B(N+1)=X make these differences empty for r greater than N. Restrict the covering disjoint family to Fin(N+1). This also covers N=0 and the empty base.

Each remaining difference A_i is compact by the compact-intersection assertion for Z, taking the open W=X. For every k, the complement of Z(k) equals the finite union of those A_i with k at most i: the cover supplies i for any point, and monotonicity decides whether that point is in Z(k). Therefore the complement is a compact open. In a quasi-separated space a compact open is retrocompact and constructible (Mathlib IsCompact.isConstructible); constructibility is closed under complement and difference. Hence every Z(k) and A_i is constructible. Each A_i is locally closed as the intersection of the open complement of Z(i) and the closed Z(i+1).

Realize any locally closed subset O intersect C by taking the closed subset preimage of C in the open subscheme O, the closed subscheme defined by its vanishing ideal, and composing its closed immersion with O to X. Mathlib range_subschemeι, coe_support_vanishingIdeal, and the range of the open immersion show that the image is exactly O intersect C. A closed immersion followed by an open immersion is an immersion. Apply this construction to every A_i and assemble LocallyClosedStratification with the already proved cover, disjointness, local closedness, and constructibility.

The immersion of the i-th stratum has range A_i. Apply the universal property for Z to this immersion: its pullback of j is finite locally free of degree i, hence finite by the IsFiniteLocallyFree parent field. This proves the required finite-pullback assertion for every stratum.

lean.statement: theorem exists_constructible_stratified_finite {X U : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (j : U ⟶ X) [Flat j] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation j] [IsSeparated j] (hj : j.IsQuasiFinite) : ∃ S : LocallyClosedStratification X, (∀ i : Fin S.n, Topology.IsConstructible (S.stratum i)) ∧ (∀ i : Fin S.n, IsFinite (pullback.snd j (S.immersion i)))
